question.html:
A girl pushes a toy car of mass 0.12 kg on a flat, frictionless surface. The car starts from rest and it reaches a speed of 2.5 m s. The toy car is in contact with the girl's hand for 267 ms.

a.

i. Calculate the average force exerted by the girl's hand on the car.

  [2]

ii. State how Newton's third law applies as the girl pushes the toy car. 

  [1]

b. After the girl pushes the car, it collides with a stationary wooden block. The direction of the car's momentum does not change, but its magnitude decreases by 60%. The speed of the wooden block after the collision is 2.6 m s.

i. Show that the mass of the wooden block is approximately 70 g.

  [3]

ii. State one similarity and one difference between an inelastic and an elastic collision.

  [2]

iii. Deduce that the collision between the toy car and the block is inelastic.

  [3] 

c. The girl pushes the toy car a second time along the same, frictionless surface. After the car loses contact with the girl's hand it reaches a ramp. At this moment, the car's wheels are blocked and stop turning, so the car slides up the ramp. The ramp makes an angle of with the horizontal. The dynamic friction coefficient between the ramp's surface and the wheels of the car is . Assume that all wheels experience the same normal reaction force and friction force.

i. Draw a fully labeled free-body diagram to represent the forces acting on the toy car as it travels up the ramp.

  [3]

ii. Calculate the magnitude of the net force acting on the toy car as it travels up the ramp.

  [3]
